Sauces

Make two per week. Click a sauce for the recipe and best pairings.

Pura Vida–ish cilantro

Creamy, herby, tangy and gently sweet.

Recipe + pairings

Blend ½ cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt, a large handful of cilantro, 1 Tbsp each olive oil and lemon juice, 1 tsp each Dijon, GF tamari and honey, plus chili and salt.

Use with: salmon, tofu, turkey, broccoli, corn and feta.

Egg-free spicy aioli

The creamy heat for shrimp, tofu and salmon.

Recipe + pairings

Blend ½ cup cottage cheese or Greek yogurt with 1–2 Tbsp GF hot sauce, lime juice, salt and a splash of olive oil. Vegan mayo gives a more classic texture.

Use with: spicy salmon, shrimp, tofu and Mexican bowls.

Lemon-herb tahini

Bright enough for fish; substantial enough for vegetables.

Recipe + pairings

Whisk ¼ cup tahini with one lemon, 2–4 Tbsp cold water, a splash of olive oil, salt, chili and parsley, dill or cilantro.

Use with: haddock, bass, chickpeas, cauliflower and feta.

Spicy soy-ginger

Salty, sharp and fresh—not heavy.

Recipe + pairings

Whisk 2 Tbsp GF tamari, 1 Tbsp rice vinegar, lime, grated ginger, 1 tsp sesame oil and chili. Thin with water to taste.

Use with: shrimp, tofu, salmon, cucumber and carrots.

Egg-free Caesar

A sharp, creamy bridge between greens and broccoli.

Recipe + pairings

Blend ½ cup Greek yogurt or cottage cheese with lemon, Dijon, parmesan, garlic, black pepper and enough water to pour. Add capers for extra savory flavor.

Use with: romaine, broccoli, Brussels sprouts, Pacha croutons and any simple protein.

Spicy cilantro-lime

The shortcut from bowl to taco-night flavor.

Recipe + pairings

Blend ½ cup yogurt or cottage cheese with cilantro, lime, jalapeño or hot sauce, cumin and salt.

Use with: turkey, corn, avocado, cauliflower and black beans.

Smoky roasted corn

The important move is drying the corn and letting it sit long enough to char. Lime goes on after cooking.

Skillet method · best char

For 2 cups of corn

  1. Thaw frozen corn, or drain canned corn. Pat it very dry.
  2. Heat a wide cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium-high until properly hot.
  3. Toss corn with 1 teaspoon olive oil, ½ teaspoon smoked paprika, ¼ teaspoon cumin, chili and salt.
  4. Add it in one layer. Leave it untouched for 2–3 minutes, then stir and cook another 4–5 minutes.
  5. Finish off the heat with lime and chopped cilantro. Add feta only after it cools slightly.
Oven method · hands-off

For a larger batch

Heat the oven and an empty sheet pan to 450°F / 230°C. Toss dry corn with oil and seasonings, spread it onto the hot pan, and roast for 15–20 minutes. Stir once near the end.

Make it more smoky

Add a pinch of chipotle powder. Smoked paprika gives aroma; chipotle adds both smoke and heat.

Keep it from steaming

Use a wide pan, dry the corn thoroughly, and avoid crowding. A packed pan traps moisture instead of browning.

Fruit pairings

Use fruit as a bright accent—about ¼ to ⅓ cup per bowl—then balance its sweetness with pickle, citrus, herbs or chili.

01 · lush + spicy

Mango + salmon

Cilantro, cucumber, pickled onion

Add avocado, cashews or hemp, then finish with spicy aioli and tamari-lime.

02 · tart + salty

Pomegranate + salmon or haddock

Feta, parsley, pickled red onion

Finish with walnuts and lemon-herb tahini. Keep the arils fresh rather than pickling them.

03 · sweet + ginger

Pineapple + shrimp, tofu or chicken

Cucumber, carrot, scallion

Add cashews and spicy soy-ginger dressing. Char the pineapple if the rest of the bowl is warm.

04 · citrus + savory

Orange + tuna, sardines or bass

Cucumber, tomato, basil or dill

Add walnuts and a sharp lemon-Dijon vinaigrette. Remove the white pith for a cleaner flavor.

05 · crisp + creamy

Apple + chicken salad

Celery, dill, cornichons

Add walnuts and a cottage-cheese Dijon dressing. A tart, crisp apple works best.

06 · juicy + peppery

Peach + shrimp or tofu

Basil, cucumber, pickled carrot

Add cashews and chili-lime dressing. Grill the peach when you want a warmer bowl.

Master refrigerator brine

½ cup vinegar
½ cup water
1 tsp salt
1–2 tsp honey or sugar

Warm just enough to dissolve, pour over sliced vegetables, cool and refrigerate. Taste after 30 minutes; the flavor deepens overnight.

Favorite combination: pickled red onion + fresh pomegranate + feta + walnuts + parsley.

Scoop bowls

Make the protein salad ahead, then place one scoop onto greens and vegetables.

Tuna–cornichon scoop

Tuna + celery + cornichons + Dijon + lemon + cottage cheese or Greek yogurt + dill or parsley + chili.

Turn it into a bowl

Add romaine, cucumber, tomatoes, Pacha toast, walnuts, hemp seeds and a little lemon-Dijon dressing.

Lemon-herb chicken scoop

Chopped chicken + celery + cucumber or cornichons + feta + lemon + olive oil + dill + parsley + walnuts.

Turn it into a bowl

Add romaine, roasted cauliflower, tomato, pickled carrot, Pacha toast and lemon tahini.

Nuts & seeds

Use what is already in the kitchen. One or two crunches per bowl is plenty.

Walnuts

Mediterranean, Italian, Caesar and salmon bowls. Toast briefly for better flavor.

Cashews

Asian and spicy bowls, or soaked and blended into creamy sauces.

Hemp seeds

The easiest universal sprinkle. Especially good on salmon, tofu and scoop bowls.

Ground flax

Mix into tuna salad, chicken salad, dressing or bread. Grind before using.

Chia + basil seeds

Best hydrated or baked into bread. They gel quickly, so they are not ideal dry crunches.

Brazil nuts

Finely grate or chop one occasionally. They are exceptionally selenium-rich, so they are not a handful-style topping.

Comfort note: Don’t stack a huge serving of crucifers, beans, chia, flax and several nuts in one bowl. Increase fiber gradually, and test one legume at a time.

Flourless buckwheat bread

Dense, moist and best toasted—ideal beside a bowl or cut into croutons.

Ingredients

2 cups raw buckwheat groats
¾–1 cup fresh water
2 Tbsp ground flax
1 Tbsp chia
1 tsp salt
1 tsp gluten-free baking powder

Optional: ¼ cup pumpkin seeds, hemp seeds or chopped walnuts.

Method

  1. Soak the raw groats in plenty of water for 4–6 hours.
  2. Drain, rinse and blend with ¾ cup fresh water into a thick batter.
  3. Stir in flax, chia, salt, baking powder and optional seeds.
  4. Rest 15 minutes. Add a splash of water only if extremely stiff.
  5. Bake in a lined small loaf pan at 350°F / 175°C for 55–65 minutes.
  6. Cool completely before slicing. Refrigerate or freeze, then toast.
